name: Wilmington Ridge/Whiteface Mountain Trail
quote: Whiteface Mountain (4,867 feet) can be summited using the Wilmington Ridge/Whiteface Mountain Trail which ascends nearly 3,700 feet and traverses 5.2 mile from the trailhead to the summit of the mountain.
why: Long ridge climb from Wilmington to the summit of Whiteface; 5.2 mi one-way doubled.

name: Ridge Trail/ Zander Scott Trail
quote: The trail extends approximately 3 miles and ascends 3,050 feet from the Zander Scott Trailhead to the summit.
why: Main route up Giant Mountain along an open rock ridge, passing Giant's Washbowl; about 3 mi one-way doubled.

name: Roaring Brook Trail
quote: The trail extends 3.4 miles and ascends 3,375 feet from the Roaring Brook Trailhead to the summit.
why: Alternate climb of Giant Mountain past the top of Roaring Brook Falls; 3.4 mi one-way doubled.

name: Rocky Peak Ridge (East Trail to Giant)
quote: The 6.7-mile trail ascends 3,600 feet.
why: Long day climb from Route 9 over Blueberry Cobbles and Bald Mountain to the high point of Rocky Peak Ridge; 6.7 mi one-way doubled.

name: Hurricane Mountain Trail from 9N
quote: The trail ascends approximately 2,000 feet over 3.4 miles from the Route 9N Trailhead to the summit.
why: Rough, steep-in-places route to the fire-tower summit of Hurricane Mountain; 3.4 mi one-way doubled.

name: East Hurricane Mountain Trail
quote: The trail ascends 1,700 feet over 2.7 miles from the Hurricane Mountain Lane Trailhead.
why: Shortest route to Hurricane Mountain via the former observer road; 2.7 mi one-way doubled.

name: North Trail
quote: The trail ascends 1,600 feet along the 3-mile trail to the summit.
why: Moderate-grade approach to Hurricane Mountain from Crow's Clearing; 3 mi one-way doubled.

name: Soda Range
quote: A 6.0-mile loop begins at the Crow's Clearing Trailhead and ascends a total of 1,600 feet.
why: Loop over Big Crow and Weston Mountain along the ledgy Nun-da-ga-o Ridge.

name: McKenzie Mountain
quote: The trail extends 5.2 miles from the Ray Brook Trailhead and ascends 2,195 feet to the summit.
why: Climb to McKenzie Mountain from Ray Brook, flat at first and steep at the end; 5.2 mi one-way doubled.

name: Haystack Mountain
quote: Haystack Mountain (2,874 feet) extends 3.3 miles and ascends 1,210 feet from the Ray Brook Trailhead.
why: Branch off the McKenzie trail to a summit with western views; 3.3 mi one-way doubled.

name: Baker Mountain
quote: The trail extends 0.9 mile and ascends nearly 900 feet from the trailhead to the summit.
why: Short Saranac Lake climb that DEC calls the wilderness's most popular hike; 0.9 mi one-way doubled.

name: Pitchoff Mountain (3,600 ft.) Trail
quote: The trail ascends 1.9 miles and 1,400 feet from the Pitchoff Mountain West Trailhead.
why: Climb from Route 73 past the Balanced Boulders to Pitchoff's summit; 1.9 mi one-way doubled. The full traverse is 'extends 4.3 miles over the summit between two trailheads' (point-to-point, 6.9 km).

name: Blue Mountain Trail
quote: Blue Mountain Trail (3,760 feet) extends 2.2 miles and ascends 1,550 feet from the trailhead on State Route 30
why: Climb to the public fire tower on Blue Mountain above Blue Mountain Lake; 2.2 mi one-way doubled.

name: Hadley Mountain Trail
quote: The 1.4-mile trail is a very popular hiking trail to an open summit with spectacular views, an historic fire tower and a ranger cabin.
why: Short, steep, family-favourite climb to an open fire-tower summit; 1.4 mi one-way doubled.

name: Observer's Trail (Poke-O-Moonshine Mountain)
quote: The 1.9-mile Observer's Trail which ascends 1,280 feet from the trailhead (Google Maps) to the summit
why: Old fire-observer road past beaver ponds to the Poke-O-Moonshine fire tower; 1.9 mi one-way doubled.

name: Ranger Trail (Poke-O-Moonshine Mountain)
quote: The 1.8-mile Ranger Trail ascends 1,280 feet from the trailhead (Google Maps) in the Poke-O-Moonshine Day Use Area to the summit.
why: Rebuilt, stone-stepped route to the same fire tower; 1.8 mi one-way doubled.

name: Prospect Mountain Trail
quote: The trail starts from Smith Street in Lake George Village and ascends 1,570 feet and 1.7 miles to the top of Prospect Mountain
why: Climb from Lake George Village to the top of Prospect Mountain; 1.7 mi one-way doubled.

name: Sleeping Beauty Mountain
quote: The trail ascends 1,038 feet and 2.1 miles from the Dacy Clearing Parking Area to the summit at 2,347 feet.
why: Climb from Dacy Clearing to the Sleeping Beauty summit above Lake George; 2.1 mi one-way doubled.

name: Buck Mountain Trail
quote: After the stream crossing, follow the yellow trail to the summit (6.6 miles round trip).
why: Summit hike from the Pilot Knob trailhead with views over Lake George. The same page gives a '3.2 miles round trip' moderate loop option.

name: Fifth Peak
quote: It is a 2.8 mile one way trip with an elevation gain of over 1400 feet for this hike.
why: Popular Tongue Mountain Range hike to a lean-to and views of Lake George; 2.8 mi one-way doubled.

name: Crane Mountain Trail
quote: The 1.75-mile Crane Mountain Trail begins at the parking lot at the end of Ski Hi Road.
why: Very steep climb with ladders to the open ridgeline of the southern Adirondacks' highest peak; 1.75 mi one-way doubled.

name: Catamount Mountain
quote: The summit can be reached via a 1.8-mile trail that ascends 1,540 feet from the trailhead.
why: Climb with an exposed scramble to a blueberry-covered summit; 1.8 mi one-way doubled.

name: Azure Mountain
quote: Azure Mountain (2,518 feet) is a 1.0-mile hike that climbs 944 feet to the summit of the mountain
why: Short climb to a summit fire tower with 360-degree views; 1.0 mi one-way doubled.

name: Bald Mountain (Rondaxe Fire Tower)
quote: Don't expect to be alone during this nearly two-mile round-trip hike
why: Popular bedrock-ridge walk near Old Forge to the restored Rondaxe fire tower. The page says 'just under a mile' and 'about 500 feet' to the summit, and 'nearly two-mile round-trip'; km uses 2 mi.

name: Mt. Arab
quote: This 1-mile, one way, hike gains 750 feet from the trailhead (Google Maps) to the summit of Mount Arab.
why: Short climb near Tupper Lake to a summit fire tower; 1 mi one-way doubled.
